transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Well… mostly I’ve been feeling foggy in my head. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, dates for exhibits, and whether I’ve already called a volunteer. It’s been bothering me.
How long have you been feeling this foggy sensation in your head?
About four months, I guess. It seemed to start after the water damage, when the remodel began.
Has this foggy feeling been interfering with your daily activities or work?

Yes… it has. I’ve missed some doctor visits, and I got the senior center schedule all mixed up. My husband’s had to help with the calls and calendars… and even decisions about the repairs that I used to handle myself.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened before the water damage and remodel began?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really noticed much from before that. It’s more the recent things that get mixed up.
Do you ever feel unsure about where you are or what time of day it is?
Not really… I mean, I don’t think so. I know where I am. The time can get a little fuzzy, but not like I don’t know if it’s morning or night.
Do you ever feel unsure about who you are?
No… I don’t think so. I know who I am.
Have you been having trouble learning new things, like picking up a new hobby or learning a new skill, since you started feeling foggy?
I haven’t really tried to learn a new hobby or anything. It’s more… my head feels foggy, and I mix up simple things, like appointment times or dates, or who I already called.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you're talking to someone?
I don’t think so… not in any big way. Sometimes I pause a little, but I haven’t really noticed not being able to find words.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or personality since you started feeling foggy?

Maybe… yes. When the house work first started, I felt sort of charged up, more than usual. Almost good, I guess. But I was also short with people… my husband, and some of the young volunteers, if they questioned what I wanted done.
Have you been feeling anxious or nervous since the water damage and remodel began?
I don’t know… maybe a little on edge with all the mess, but I wouldn’t say nervous exactly. It’s just been a lot.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed since the water damage and remodel began?
Not really sad, no… not depressed like that. It’s been frustrating, and I get tired of it, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been down.
Do you ever feel disoriented or unsure about your surroundings?
Not really… I mean, I know where I am. I don’t think I’ve been confused about that. Maybe just foggy, but not lost or anything.
Have you had any physical health problems since the water damage and remodel began?
I’m not sure… nothing really comes to mind. I mean, I’m older, so there’s always little things, but I haven’t noticed anything new because of the remodel.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since the water damage and remodel began?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed anything different. Sleep’s been about the same, I guess.
Have you noticed any changes in your interests or how you interact with others since you started feeling foggy?

I guess… yes. I don’t really feel like doing much of anything. My watercolors, my tomato plants, line dancing… even watching the cardinals out back. Those used to matter to me, and now they just kind of sit there. I can’t seem to make myself care.
Have you been seeing or hearing things that aren't really there?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t been seeing or hearing anything like that.
Have you noticed any difficulty with tasks that require planning or organization?

Yes… that’s mostly what brought me in. My head feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates… sometimes I can’t remember which volunteer I already called. It’s embarrassing.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your personality since the water damage and remodel began?

A little, maybe. When the work on the house first started, I felt… unusually charged up, like I could handle everything. But I was sharper with people than I like to admit. I’d snap at my husband, or at the younger volunteers, if they questioned what I wanted done.
Do you have trouble recalling important details about your life, such as your address or your husband's name?
No… not things like that. I know where I live, and of course I know my husband’s name. It’s more… smaller things that get jumbled.
Have you had trouble remembering your past or significant life events?
Not really… I mean, I remember the big things. My wedding, raising my family, places we lived. I don’t think those have gone missing. It’s more that I don’t always like being put on the spot.
